sam: Heads-up — I found a deterministic output delta after the batching heuristic change (PR #342). FP8 matmul + activation quant path diverges on mixed short/long batches.

lisa: Which model / config? can you paste repro command?

sam: repro is small: `./run_infer --model=redwood-rls-3b --seqs=512,16,16 --batching=dynamic --quant=fp8 --act-quant=true --seed=42`

kevin: saw something similar on a different branch. Output diff shows errors concentrated in early layers (attn q/k matmul).

perf-bot: profiler snapshot attached:
```
Kernel breakdown:
matmul_fp8_kern_v2         34.2ms  41.1%   (used for seq>=128)
matmul_fp16_kern_fast      12.1ms  14.5%   (used for seq<128)
act_quantize_fp8           6.8ms   8.2%    (per-batch calibration)
kv_write                    2.2ms  2.6%    (cache writes)
Other                      22.0ms  26.6%
```
Notice: when dynamic batching picks fp8_kern_v2 for long rows and fp16 for short rows we get mixed kernel results.
```
(profiler capture id: perf-1764528)
```

nitya: Hypothesis: activation quant step uses per-batch calibrator state that isn't being cleared when micro-batches are fused into a larger batch. The matmul kernel selection then interleaves FP8 and FP16 kernels while the calibrator's running min/max are contaminated by previous micro-batch scales. That can change quantization scales and hence bit-level outputs.

sam: Confirmed: forcing `--quant-reset-per-microbatch=true` makes outputs bit-identical to pre-PR behavior. Static padding (pad to max seq and use single kernel) also matches. So it's a state leak in the activation calibrator across fused micro-batches.

lisa: Nice find. What's the perf impact of resetting per micro-batch?

sam: Perf numbers (same run):
```
before (PR#342):     89.4 tokens/s
with reset flag:       83.9 tokens/s  (-6.1%)
static-pad (single):  84.5 tokens/s  (-5.5%)
```
So correctness fix costs ~5-6% unless we find a smarter handler.

kevin: Idea: track a compact "scale fingerprint" in the KV cache header per layer. When kernels switch, consult header to see if scale live differs; if mismatch, force kernel-aligned recalibration only for affected layers. That avoids full recalibration for every micro-batch.

nitya: Agree — we already store a 64-bit key for kv-checkpoint. Reuse it: append a `quant_scale_id` per layer. On write, set to current scale; on read, if `quant_scale_id != expected` trigger micro-recalib for that layer only.

sam: I'll prototype: small patch in activation_quantizer that exposes `current_scale_id()` and a fast compare in kv_writer. If miss, we run `recalib_layer(layer_idx, input_slice)` which is cheap (a single tensor min/max + affine compute).

lisa: Add unit/regression: mix seq lengths 8/128/512 interleaved for 1000 steps and assert L2 < 1e-6 and top-k tokens equal.

kevin: Also add a kernel-selection policy tweak: prefer same-kernel-as-last-for that sequence slot if the scale_id matches to reduce kernel thrashing.

sam: Opening issue + canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/418 (WIP). Patch implements scale_id KV header + per-layer recalib fallback.

nitya: Can you add a simple perf microbenchmark to measure recalib cost separately (one layer, varying hidden=1024..8192)? We need a tighter cost model before landing.

sam: Will do. Repro artifact and logs in the issue. Thanks all — will follow up with bench numbers and a canary earlier this week. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: automated note — regression test queued: reg-1764528-quant-leak. Results expected in ~30m.

lisa: nice triage. tagging @oncall-runtime for visibility.

kevin: one more thing — check quant calibration RNG seed, different micro-batch order can still alter running min/max if nondeterministic. Make calibration deterministic if we rely on cache-match optimizations.

sam: good call. seeding added to the PR.

nitya: sweet. also add comment explaining why we prefer scale_id compare over recompute always. saves perf and clarifies KV compatibility semantics.

sam: merging to canary after perf microbench. will post results here.
